macho_grams_gramsbe_savage Grower A: “60/60
preserves terps.”
Grower B: "70/55 gives you louder flower.”
What if | told you... you're BOTH right?
The idea is that a cooler, controlled drying environment
can slow the rate at which volatile compounds escape,
while also slowing moisture removal compared with a
warmer, drier environment.
At a warmer drying temperature, some of the more
volatile aromatic compounds can move into the air more
readily. That can make the aroma you perceive at the
moment seem stronger, even if some of those same
compounds are being lost from the flower.
And here's the part that gets overlooked:
LOUDER DOESN'T AUTOMATICALLY MEAN MORE
TERPENES.
What you smell during or immediately after drying is not
necessarily the same thing as what remains in the
flower.
The real variable is TIME.
Temperature x RH x Airflow x Time = The drying
environment
So which is better?
That depends on what you're optimizing for and what
happens to the flower over the entire process.
